recent_posts.title: The Browser Is Breaking Your DLP: How Data Slips Past Modern Controls
recent_posts.summary: Traditional DLP solutions have a critical blind spot: the browser. As enterprise workflows shift to browser-based apps like Google Workspace, GitHub, and AI tools such as ChatGPT, sensitive data increasingly moves through copy/paste actions, form inputs, AI prompts, and file uploads to unsanctioned accounts — all invisible to endpoint and network DLP. Analysis shows 46% of sensitive file uploads go to unsanctioned accounts. Browser-native DLP, as offered by Keep Aware, addresses this gap by operating directly within browsing sessions to inspect clipboard activity, form inputs, and uploads in real time, with full account and application context to enforce inline policies.

recent_posts.title: Hackers abuse Google ads for GoDaddy ManageWP login phishing
recent_posts.summary: A phishing campaign is abusing Google sponsored search results to target ManageWP credentials. The attack uses an adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) setup where a fake login page proxies credentials in real-time to the attacker, including 2FA codes, allowing full account takeover. Each compromised ManageWP account can expose hundreds of WordPress sites. Guardio Labs infiltrated the attacker's C2 infrastructure, found a private phishing framework with Russian-language disclaimers, and has identified at least 200 victims so far.

recent_posts.title: Palo Alto Networks warns of firewall RCE zero-day exploited in attacks
recent_posts.summary: Palo Alto Networks has disclosed a critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-0300) in the PAN-OS User-ID Authentication Portal, currently being actively exploited. The flaw is a buffer overflow that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on internet-exposed PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls. Over 5,800 PAN-OS VM-series firewalls are currently exposed online. No patch is available yet; the company strongly recommends restricting portal access to trusted zones only or disabling it entirely. This is the latest in a series of PAN-OS zero-days exploited in the wild.

recent_posts.title: Google now offers up to $1.5 million for some Android exploits
recent_posts.summary: Google has overhauled its Android and Chrome Vulnerability Rewards Programs, raising top bounties to $1.5 million for zero-click Pixel Titan M2 full-chain exploits with persistence. Chrome full-chain browser process exploits now earn up to $250,000 plus a $250,128 bonus for MiraclePtr-protected memory exploits. Simultaneously, Google is scaling back payouts for vulnerabilities that AI has made easier to discover, shifting focus to concise proof-of-concept reports rather than lengthy write-ups. The Android program will narrow its scope to Linux kernel vulnerabilities in Google-maintained components unless concrete Android exploitability is demonstrated. This restructuring follows a record $17.1 million paid to 747 researchers in 2025, bringing total program payouts since 2010 to over $81.6 million.

recent_posts.title: Karakurt extortion gang ‘cold case’ negotiator gets 8.5 years in prison
recent_posts.summary: Deniss Zolotarjovs, a Latvian national and member of the Russian Karakurt ransomware group, has been sentenced to 8.5 years in prison in the United States. His role was as a 'cold case' negotiator — re-engaging victims who had stopped communicating without paying ransom — and he used stolen personal and health data to increase psychological pressure. The FBI linked him to at least six extortion cases against American organizations between 2021 and 2023. Karakurt, led by former Conti gang leaders, attacked over 54 companies resulting in losses exceeding $56 million from just 13 known victims. Zolotarjovs is the first Karakurt member to be charged and sentenced in the U.S.

recent_posts.title: Amazon SES increasingly abused in phishing to evade detection
recent_posts.summary: Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) is being increasingly exploited by threat actors to send phishing emails that bypass SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication checks. The main driver is the growing exposure of AWS IAM access keys in public GitHub repos, .ENV files, Docker images, and S3 buckets. Attackers use automated tools like TruffleHog to find leaked credentials, validate permissions, and mass-distribute phishing emails. Attack types include fake DocuSign notifications and business email compromise (BEC) campaigns with fabricated invoice threads. Because SES is a legitimate service, IP-based blocking is impractical. Kaspersky recommends least-privilege IAM policies, MFA, key rotation, and IP-based access restrictions.

recent_posts.title: Backdoored PyTorch Lightning package drops credential stealer
recent_posts.summary: A malicious version of PyTorch Lightning (v2.6.3) was published on PyPI containing a hidden execution chain that silently downloads a JavaScript runtime (Bun) and executes a heavily obfuscated 11.4 MB payload upon import. The malware, dubbed 'ShaiWorm' by Microsoft Defender, steals credentials from .env files, API keys, GitHub tokens, browser data (Chrome, Firefox, Brave), and cloud service credentials (AWS, Azure, GCP). Microsoft Threat Intelligence detected and blocked the activity on customer environments. The package has been reverted to the safe v2.6.1. Users who ran 'import lightning' with v2.6.3 are advised to immediately rotate all secrets and tokens. The investigation into how the build/release pipeline was compromised is ongoing.

recent_posts.title: Trellix discloses data breach after source code repository hack
recent_posts.summary: Cybersecurity firm Trellix has disclosed a data breach in which attackers gained unauthorized access to a portion of its source code repository. The company, formed from the 2021 merger of McAfee Enterprise and FireEye, is working with forensic experts and has notified law enforcement. So far, no evidence has been found that the source code was exploited or that release/distribution processes were affected. Trellix joins a growing list of cybersecurity companies breached recently, including Checkmarx (LAPSUS$ group) and Cisco (Trivy supply chain attack).

recent_posts.title: They don’t hack, they borrow: How fraudsters target credit unions
recent_posts.summary: Underground forums are circulating structured loan fraud methods targeting small and mid-sized credit unions. Fraudsters use stolen personal data to pass knowledge-based authentication (KBA) checks and submit fraudulent loan applications without exploiting any software vulnerabilities. The 8-step workflow covers identity acquisition, credit profile assessment, KBA preparation, target selection, application submission, verification bypass, loan approval, and rapid cash-out through intermediary accounts. Smaller credit unions are preferred targets due to perceived weaker fraud detection and reliance on traditional verification. Fraud exposure in auto lending alone is projected at $9.2 billion in 2025. Flare, the article's sponsor, offers dark web monitoring to detect stolen identity data before it is weaponized.

recent_posts.title: Progress warns of critical MOVEit Automation auth bypass flaw
recent_posts.summary: Progress Software has disclosed a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-4670) in MOVEit Automation, its enterprise managed file transfer product. The flaw can be exploited remotely without privileges or user interaction, affecting versions before 2025.1.5, 2025.0.9, and 2024.1.8. A high-severity privilege escalation bug (CVE-2026-5174) was also patched simultaneously. Over 1,400 MOVEit Automation instances are exposed online, including systems linked to U.S. government agencies. The only remediation is upgrading to a patched release using the full installer. While no active exploitation has been confirmed, MOVEit has historically been a high-value target — the Clop ransomware gang exploited a MOVEit Transfer zero-day in 2023, impacting over 2,100 organizations and 62 million individuals.
